title: Natural constant models from scalar-normalized module equivalences
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in the coefficient universe with exact abelian sheafification and the closed sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $R$ a commutative ring object of $\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$, supplied with a ring-object map $\sigma:\underline B\to R$. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let
$$E:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$$
be an additive equivalence and fix $t:E(R)\cong\underline B$ such that, for every $b\in B$, $tE(\sigma(b)\cdot-)t^{-1}$ is multiplication by $b$ on $\underline B$. For a $B$-module $P$, let $M_R(P)=R\otimes_{\underline B}\underline P$ be extension of internal scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], where $\underline P$ is sheafification of the constant module presheaf. A finitely presented $B$-module means a module admitting an exact sequence $B^m\xrightarrow{q}B^n\to P\to0$ for finite $m,n$. There are isomorphisms
$$\theta_P:E(M_R(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline P$$
natural in every linear map between finitely presented $B$-modules. For every such presentation, $\theta_P$ identifies the transported cokernel of the scalar matrix $\sigma(q):R^m\to R^n$ with the sheafified constant cokernel of $q:B^m\to B^n$, using $t$ on each free summand. The isomorphism is independent of the presentation and is the unique natural comparison with this normalization on finite free modules. If additive equivalences $E_U$ and regular-module identifications $t_U$ are supplied on each localized site $C/U$, together with coherent isomorphisms $E_U(M|_U)\cong E(M)|_U$ preserving these regular-module identifications and scalar endomorphisms, then the $\theta_P$ commute with all further localizations [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Consequently, on any specified covering family the existence of local models $M_{R|_U}(P_U)$ with finitely presented $P_U$ is equivalent to the existence of the corresponding constant local models $\underline{P_U}$ after applying $E$. Neither finiteness of $B$ nor a Noetherian or enough-points hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent-written natural finite-presentation comparison under scalar-normalized equivalences, serving original step 9.

proof.text: Write $C_B(P)$ for the internal $\underline B$-module obtained by sheafifying the constant module presheaf, and $G(P)$ for its fixed-$B$ module-valued version. Module sheafification extends the action uniquely and has the factorization property of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]; [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves] identifies the section-ring and fixed-$B$ versions with their underlying sheaves unchanged. For a linear map $q$, the constant presheaf of $\operatorname{coker}q$ is its pointwise cokernel; the assumed exact abelian sheafification gives the same cokernel on underlying abelian sheaves. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $\underline B\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits, so [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels] makes that sheafified quotient a cokernel in internal $\underline B$-modules. In the section-ring version the same quotient is a module cokernel: a map killing $q$ factors uniquely through it by module sheafification's factorization property; the fixed-$B$ equivalence then gives the assertion for $G$. Finite sums are sheafifications of the finite sums of constant presheaves, with the same inclusions and projections. Thus $C_B$ and $G$ preserve finite sums and cokernels, and $C_B(B)=\underline B$, $G(B)=\underline B$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact; agent application to constant presheaves and internal cokernels

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], $T=\operatorname{Ext}_\sigma$ preserves finite colimits. Its hypotheses hold: the sheaf tensor is braided and closed, hence preserves colimits in each variable, and both coefficient rings are commutative. The balancing coequalizer identifies $T(\underline B)$ with $R$: the action map is $r\otimes b\mapsto r\sigma(b)$, with inverse induced by $r\mapsto r\otimes1$; balancing gives the inverse equations. These are equations of the sheaf tensor maps, so they descend from presheaves. In particular $M_R(B^n)\cong R^n$ with its standard summands. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], $E$ preserves finite sums and cokernels. Set $F=E\circ T\circ C_B$. Both $F$ and $G$ therefore preserve finite sums and cokernels.

source.place: Extension clause (2), the balancing coequalizer and finite-colimit preservation; categories.tex Tag 0038 for the equivalence

proof.text: Let $t_n:F(B^n)\cong G(B^n)$ be the finite-sum extension of $t$, using the regular-module identification of step 2. For any scalar matrix $q=(q_{ij}):B^m\to B^n$, its extension is $\sigma(q)=\sum_{i,j}\iota_i\,\sigma(q_{ij})\,p_j$. An additive functor takes this expression to the same sum of the images of its factors. The definition of $t_n$ identifies the summand inclusions and projections, and the hypothesis on $t$ identifies the middle factor with multiplication by $q_{ij}$. Consequently $t_n F(q)=G(q)t_m$. Empty sums give the same equality when $m=0$ or $n=0$.

source.place: Agent matrix computation using the stated scalar normalization and finite biproduct identities

proof.text: Choose a presentation $B^m\xrightarrow{q}B^n\xrightarrow{\pi}P\to0$. By steps 1 and 2, $F(\pi)$ and $G(\pi)$ are cokernels of $F(q)$ and $G(q)$. Step 3 shows that $G(\pi)t_n$ kills $F(q)$, giving a unique $\theta_{P,\pi}$ with $\theta_{P,\pi}F(\pi)=G(\pi)t_n$. Conversely $F(\pi)t_n^{-1}$ kills $G(q)$ and gives an inverse: both composites are identities after precomposition with their cokernel projections, which are epimorphisms. Thus this is an isomorphism identifying precisely the two specified cokernel projections.

source.place: Agent use of the cokernel universal property after Tag 03CY and the matrix computation

proof.text: For a linear map $f:P\to Q$ and presentations with surjections $\pi:B^n\to P$ and $\pi':B^{n'}\to Q$, choose, for each basis vector $e_j$ of $B^n$, a vector $a_j\in B^{n'}$ with $\pi'(a_j)=f\pi(e_j)$. Such vectors exist by surjectivity of the ordinary module map $\pi'$. The matrix $A$ with columns $a_j$ satisfies $\pi'A=f\pi$. This lifts only a map of ordinary finite free $B$-modules; it makes no assertion that constant free sheaves are projective.

source.place: Agent finite-basis lifting in ordinary modules

proof.text:
Precomposing with $F(\pi)$, use steps 3–5 to calculate
$$\theta_{Q,\pi'}F(f)F(\pi)=G(\pi')t_{n'}F(A)=G(\pi')G(A)t_n=G(f)G(\pi)t_n=G(f)\theta_{P,\pi}F(\pi).$$
Since $F(\pi)$ is a cokernel projection and hence an epimorphism, this proves naturality for $f$. The calculation uses only $\pi'A=f\pi$, so it works for every choice of the lifts, without a lifting of the relation modules.

source.place: Agent explicit naturality equation for the quotient comparison

proof.text: Apply step 6 to $f=\mathrm{id}_P$ and any two finite presentations of $P$. Both functors send this identity to an identity, so $\theta_{P,\pi}=\theta_{P,\pi'}$. Define $\theta_P$ by this presentation-independent value. On $B^n$, use the presentation $0\to B^n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}B^n\to0$ to obtain $\theta_{B^n}=t_n$. If $\eta:F\to G$ is any natural comparison with these free-module components, naturality for $\pi:B^n\to P$ forces $\eta_P F(\pi)=G(\pi)t_n$ and hence $\eta_P=\theta_P$. This proves the asserted uniqueness, as well as the normalization for every presentation.

source.place: Agent independence and uniqueness from the preceding quotient equation

proof.text: For localization, strong monoidal sheafification in step 1 makes its local equivalences stable under tensoring, as required by the internal/section-ring comparison. Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to pass between internal and section-ring modules without changing their underlying sheaves or maps. Restriction preserves finite colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-restriction-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction], restriction takes a constant module sheaf and its constant linear maps to the same constant module sheaf and maps on the slice, compatibly with their sheafification units. These statements apply to $B$, $R$ and each localized site, which are small in the same coefficient universe. The sectionwise description and relocalization in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identify $R|_U$, its regular module, and further restrictions.

source.place: Section Tag 03DH, Definition 04IX; sites.tex Tag 00XR for restriction/sheafification, Tag 03EH for relocalization

proof.text: Restrict the presentation $R^m\xrightarrow{\sigma(q)}R^n\to M_R(P)\to0$. Step 8 makes it the cokernel presentation $(R|_U)^m\xrightarrow{\sigma|_U(q)}(R|_U)^n\to M_R(P)|_U\to0$. Step 2 on $C/U$ gives exactly this presentation for $M_{R|_U}(P)$. Their unique isomorphism preserving the quotient projections is the canonical model restriction comparison: the canonical balanced map sends $r\otimes p$ to the same $r\otimes p$ on the slice and, on the standard generator indexed by $e_j$, sends $r\otimes e_j$ to $r\otimes e_j$. It therefore gives that same quotient isomorphism. Step 6 with $f=\mathrm{id}_P$ shows independence of the presentation. On successive slices the two possible composites preserve the same quotient projection, so they agree.

source.place: Agent restriction of a finite cokernel presentation; normalization by the standard generators

proof.text: Compare $\theta_P|_U$ with the comparison built using $E_U$, after the model and constant restriction isomorphisms of steps 8–9 and the supplied equivalence comparison. Both maps now have source $E_U(M_{R|_U}(P))$ and target $\underline P_{C/U}$. Precompose each with the epimorphism $E_U((R|_U)^n\to M_{R|_U}(P))$. The defining equation in step 4 gives $G_U(\pi)t_{U,n}$ for both: the supplied comparison is natural in that quotient map and preserves $t_U$ on the regular summands. Epimorphic cancellation proves equality. Repeating this calculation on $C/V$ for $V\to U$, and using the given coherence, proves compatibility with every further localization.

source.place: Agent quotient-projection test for localization compatibility; no enough-points test

proof.text: On each member $U$ of the specified covering family, an isomorphism $M|_U\cong M_{R|_U}(P_U)$ is sent by $E_U$ and $\theta_{P_U}$ to an isomorphism $E(M)|_U\cong\underline{P_U}$. Conversely such a fixed-$B$ isomorphism, composed with $\theta_{P_U}^{-1}$, lifts uniquely through the fully faithful $E_U$ to an isomorphism of internal modules; full faithfulness reflects inverses. These constructions keep both the covering family and the finitely presented modules $P_U$. Compatibility on further slices is step 10. No step uses finiteness or Noetherianity of $B$, or points of the site.

source.place: Agent application of full faithfulness on the given cover

tool_uses.why: The arbitrary-site module sheafification universal property supplies the action and quotient factorization for constant modules; this coefficient-universe tool is not supplied by the finite-shriek unit.

Its identity-on-underlying-sheaves equivalence identifies section-ring and fixed-B encodings of the constant cokernel. It is a generic coefficient-encoding tool, not a replacement for a finite-shriek step.
Underlying abelian cokernels carry the required internal module action. This general monoidal-category tool is not a geometric shriek assertion.
The generic internal/section-ring equivalence lets the slice finite-colimit theorem apply to the actual internal modules in this item.
Only its arbitrary-ring finite-colimit preservation on a slice is used to restrict the displayed matrix cokernel; the unit contains no such general localization result.
